key_insight: WorldWeaver (W^2) introduces a streaming multi-agent diffusion framework that keeps a shared world state alive across agents and viewpoints, instead of only passing along past observations. This helps generated scenes stay consistent while interactions unfold over time.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of maintaining persistent, shared world state in multi-agent and multi-view video generation. Standard autoregressive video diffusion methods condition on observation history, which makes it hard to represent a stable state that multiple agents can jointly update.
method: Uses a streaming autoregressive video diffusion pipeline for multi-agent rollouts.
Adds cross-agent world state registers to store and carry persistent state beyond observation history.
Lets the shared state evolve across agents and views, improving consistency in interactive world generation.
impact: This matters for building more reliable interactive world models, simulation systems, and embodied AI agents that need consistent memory across time and perspectives. Practitioners get a clearer path toward generating coordinated multi-agent scenes with persistent state.

paper_title: Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers
